speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have some lesions that concern you; please describe exactly what they look like, how they have changed recently, and if you have noticed any itching, bleeding, or pain. To begin our evaluation, could you tell me your age and if you have a history of skin cancer or significant sun exposure?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

I have noted your history of heavy smoking, age, and the location of the non-healing, crusty lesions on your penis and finger, which are highly suspicious for squamous cell carcinoma. To confirm this and stage the disease, I need to see the lesions directly and check for any abnormal lymph nodes. REQUEST IMAGES: Penile_and_finger_lesions. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, CBC_with_differential. REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate, ESR. REQUEST TEST: HIV_Status.
